name: 3D Gaussian Splatting optimization
text:
# 3D Gaussian Splatting optimization
Also called: 3DGS optimization, Gaussian SLAM optimization

## Overview
This family encompasses methods that jointly optimize camera poses and a 3D Gaussian scene representation from image streams, solving the problem of [simultaneous localization and mapping](#9268-slam-and-mapping.md) (SLAM) or pose estimation in dynamic or blurry scenarios. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods like [Mapping Strategies](9321-mapping-strategies.md) and [Semantic-aware mapping](12053-semantic-aware-mapping.md) by explicitly handling the differentiable rendering pipeline's gradients for pose updates, and from [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) Representation](12096-neural-radiance-field-nerf-representation.md) by using explicit Gaussian primitives rather than implicit neural fields.

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves a coupled optimization loop where the scene representation $\mathcal{R}$ (a set of 3D Gaussians $\mathcal{G}$) and camera poses $\mathbf{T}_t$ are jointly or alternately optimized. Each Gaussian $i$ is defined by mean position $\mu_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$, covariance matrix $\Sigma_i \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 3}$ (parameterized by scale $\mathbf{s}_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and rotation $\mathbf{R}_i \in SO(3)$), opacity $\alpha_i \in [0, 1]$, and color $c_i$.

The optimization objective minimizes a loss function $L$:
$$ L = L_{photo} + \lambda L_{depth} + L_{reg} $$
where $L_{photo} = || I_{rendered} - I_{captured} ||_1$ measures color difference, $L_{depth} = || D_{rendered} - D_{captured} ||_1$ measures depth difference (if available), and $L_{reg}$ includes [regularization terms](#1413-regularization-losses.md) such as scale isotropy to prevent degenerate Gaussians.

Key challenges include avoiding duplicate densification in well-reconstructed areas, mitigating map drift from accumulated pose errors, and preventing Gaussian degeneracy (overly anisotropic scales) through regularization.

## Subtopics

### [SplaTAM](9193-splatam.md)
[SplaTAM](#9193-splatam.md) is an RGB-D Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) method that represents the scene as a [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) model. It solves the problem of online mapping and tracking by jointly optimizing camera poses and Gaussian parameters using depth and photometric constraints. It is distinguished from sibling methods like [Gaussian-SLAM](#6236-slam-and-tracking.md) and [Gaussian Splatting SLAM](#10078-gaussian-splatting-slam.md) by its use of view-independent colors and a specific densification mask strategy to prevent duplicate Gaussian creation.

### [Gaussian-SLAM](9195-gaussian-slam.md)
Gaussian-SLAM is a keyframe-based Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) method that constructs a scene representation using 3D Gaussians and employs sub-map fusion to manage global consistency. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods like SplaTAM, which relies on depth-assisted [ICP](#10563-iterative-closest-point-icp.md) for tracking, by utilizing a specific [scale regularization](#9855-scale-regularization.md) loss to enforce isotropic Gaussians, thereby stabilizing the joint optimization of camera poses and map geometry.

### [Gaussian Splatting SLAM](10078-gaussian-splatting-slam.md)
Gaussian Splatting SLAM is a simultaneous localization and mapping method that jointly optimizes camera poses and a 3D Gaussian scene representation from monocular or RGB-D video streams. It distinguishes itself from siblings like [SplaTAM](9193-splatam.md) and [Gaussian-SLAM](9195-gaussian-slam.md) by explicitly enforcing isotropic scale regularization to stabilize localization and mapping, and by utilizing a covisibility-based keyframing strategy for efficient map management.

### [Differentiable Pose Estimation](12756-differentiable-pose-estimation.md)
[Differentiable pose estimation](#12756-differentiable-pose-estimation.md) optimizes camera poses by back-propagating photometric loss gradients through a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) renderer. It solves the problem of recovering accurate camera motion, particularly in scenarios involving [motion blur](#6441-motion-blur.md), by treating pose as a differentiable variable within the rendering pipeline. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like SplaTAM and Gaussian-SLAM by explicitly decoupling the pose optimization from the scene geometry update in specific implementations (e.g., Deblur-GS), utilizing a simplified gradient derivation that ignores covariance and color terms to ensure stability during short optimization steps.

### GS-SLAM
#### definition
GS-SLAM is a SLAM method that proposes an adaptive 3D Gaussian expanding strategy to add new 3D Gaussians into the training stage and delete unreliable ones with captured depths and rendered opacity values [S1]. To avoid duplicate densification, SplaTAM uses view-independent colors for Gaussians and creates a densification mask to determine whether a pixel in a new frame needs densification by considering current Gaussians and the captured depth of the new frame [S1]. For stabilizing the localization and mapping, GaussianSplattingSLAM and Gaussian-SLAM put an extra scale regularization loss on the scale of Gaussians to encourage isotropic Gaussians [S1].

#### number
On the Replica dataset, GS-SLAM achieves PSNR 31.56, SSIM 0.97, and LPIPS 0.094 [S1].

## Background
The family originates from the application of 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) to SLAM tasks, moving beyond static novel view synthesis. GS-SLAM [180] was among the first to propose adaptive 3D Gaussian expanding and deletion based on depth and opacity [S1]. SplaTAM [181] introduced view-independent colors and densification masks to prevent duplicate creation [S1]. GaussianSplattingSLAM [182] and Gaussian-SLAM [183] introduced scale regularization for isotropic Gaussians to stabilize optimization [S1]. Other methods like LIVGaussMap [184] use LiDAR for initialization, while SGS-SLAM [185], NEDS-SLAM [186], and SemGauss-SLAM [187] extend the framework with semantic or [geometric constraints](#8727-depth-and-geometry-supervision.md) [S1].
